properties.name: Yamnaya Culture
properties.description: Pastoralist culture of the Pontic–Caspian steppe whose westward expansion carried Proto-Indo-European speech and kurgan burials across Europe.

properties.name: Corded Ware Culture
properties.description: Battle-axe culture stretching from the Rhine to the Volga; associated with the spread of Indo-European languages and single-grave burial.

properties.name: Bell Beaker Culture
properties.description: Copper-using culture of Western Europe named for its bell-shaped pottery; linked to early metallurgy and long-distance exchange.

properties.name: Únětice Culture
properties.description: Early Bronze Age culture of Central Europe famous for rich bronze hoards and the Nebra sky disc.

properties.name: Minoan Civilization
properties.description: Europe's first advanced civilization on Crete — palace-complex states, Linear A script, and maritime trade across the eastern Mediterranean.

properties.name: Mycenaean Greece
properties.description: Warrior palace-states of Late Bronze Age Greece recorded in Linear B — the world of Homer's Achaeans.

properties.name: Hittite Empire
properties.description: Anatolian great power that fought Egypt at Kadesh and produced the earliest known recorded peace treaty.

properties.name: Phrygia
properties.description: Iron Age Anatolian kingdom of King Midas, famed for its wealth and tumulus burials.

properties.name: Urartu
properties.description: Mountain kingdom around Lake Van — fortress builders and rivals of Assyria.

properties.name: Phoenicia
properties.description: Seafaring city-states of the Levantine coast that spread the alphabet and founded colonies from Cyprus to Iberia.

properties.name: Greek City-States
properties.description: The polis world of Athens, Sparta and hundreds of colonies ringing the Mediterranean and Black Sea.

properties.name: Delian League (Athenian Empire)
properties.description: Athens' naval hegemony over the Aegean, financed by tribute from allied city-states.

properties.name: Spartan Hegemony
properties.description: Lacedaemon's brief dominance over Greece after the Peloponnesian War.

properties.name: Kingdom of Macedon
properties.description: Northern Greek kingdom that unified Greece and, under Alexander, conquered the Persian Empire.

properties.name: Macedonian Empire
properties.description: Alexander the Great's conquests from Greece to the Indus — the largest empire Europe had yet produced.

properties.name: Seleucid Empire
properties.description: Hellenistic successor state ruling from the Aegean to Bactria.

properties.name: Ptolemaic Kingdom
properties.description: Hellenistic Egypt of Cleopatra; Alexandria was the intellectual capital of the Mediterranean.

properties.name: Roman Republic
properties.description: The Republic that turned a city-state into the master of the Mediterranean by Caesar's day.

properties.name: Roman Empire
properties.description: The Principate at its height under Trajan — from Hadrian's Wall to the Persian Gulf, a sea at the centre.

properties.name: Gallic Empire
properties.description: Breakaway western provinces of the Crisis of the Third Century.

properties.name: Palmyrene Empire
properties.description: Zenobia's brief eastern breakaway — Egypt, Syria and Anatolia under Palmyra.

properties.name: Western Roman Empire
properties.description: The Latin half of the divided Empire; its fall in 476 conventionally closes antiquity.

properties.name: Byzantine Empire (Early)
properties.description: The Greek-speaking eastern Empire; Justinian reconquered Italy, Africa and southern Spain.

properties.name: Byzantine Empire (Macedonian)
properties.description: The medieval zenith: Basil II 'the Bulgar-Slayer' restored Byzantine power from southern Italy to Armenia.

properties.name: Byzantine Empire (Palaiologan)
properties.description: The shrunken remnant of Rome that fell to the Ottomans in 1453.

properties.name: Hunnic Empire
properties.description: Attila's steppe confederation that struck from the Danube to Gaul and extracted tribute from both Romes.

properties.name: Ostrogothic Kingdom
properties.description: Theoderic's Gothic kingdom of Italy — a bridge between Roman and Germanic worlds.

properties.name: Visigothic Kingdom
properties.description: The Gothic kingdom of Iberia that converted to Catholic Christianity and codified Roman law.

properties.name: Vandal Kingdom
properties.description: The Vandals' North African realm that sacked Rome in 455.

properties.name: Frankish Kingdom (Merovingian)
properties.description: Clovis and his successors united Gaul and pushed Frankish power east of the Rhine.

properties.name: Lombard Kingdom
properties.description: Germanic kingdom that ruled most of Italy until Charlemagne's conquest.

properties.name: Avar Khaganate
properties.description: Steppe khaganate of the Carpathian Basin that raided deep into Francia and Byzantium.

properties.name: Carolingian Empire
properties.description: Charlemagne's empire — the first political unification of Western Europe after Rome.

properties.name: East Francia
properties.description: The German stem of the Carolingian partition — kernel of the Holy Roman Empire.

properties.name: West Francia
properties.description: The western Frankish kingdom that became France.

properties.name: Middle Francia
properties.description: Lotharingia and Italy — the short-lived middle kingdom of the Carolingian partition.

properties.name: First Bulgarian Empire
properties.description: Balkan empire that rivaled Byzantium and adopted the Cyrillic script.

properties.name: Kievan Rus'
properties.description: The Varangian-founded East Slavic state from which Russia, Ukraine and Belarus descend.

properties.name: Holy Roman Empire
properties.description: The thousand-year German Reich — a loose mosaic of princes, bishops and free cities under an elected emperor.

properties.name: Kingdom of England
properties.description: The Anglo-Saxon kingdom unified by Æthelstan; later the core of the British state.

properties.name: Kingdom of France
properties.description: The Capetian and Bourbon kingdom — Europe's demographic and cultural centre for centuries.

properties.name: Al-Andalus (Umayyad)
properties.description: The Islamic emirate and caliphate of Iberia — Córdoba rivalled Baghdad in learning.

properties.name: Crown of Castile
properties.description: The dominant Iberian crown that led the Reconquista and funded Columbus.

properties.name: Crown of Aragon
properties.description: Mediterranean trading crown spanning Catalonia, Aragon, Sardinia, Sicily and Naples.

properties.name: Kingdom of Sicily
properties.description: Norman kingdom uniting Sicily and southern Italy under a cosmopolitan court.

properties.name: Republic of Venice
properties.description: The Serenissima — maritime republic that controlled Adriatic and Aegean trade for a millennium.

properties.name: Republic of Genoa
properties.description: Ligurian maritime republic; its bankers and admirals operated across the Mediterranean and Black Sea.

properties.name: Angevin Empire
properties.description: Henry II and the Lionheart's composite realm of England and western France.

properties.name: Golden Horde
properties.description: The western Mongol khanate that dominated the Russian steppe and the Volga trade.

properties.name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania
properties.description: Europe's last pagan state became a vast realm from the Baltic to the Black Sea.

properties.name: Kingdom of Poland
properties.description: The Piast and Jagiellonian kingdom of Poland.

properties.name: Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
properties.description: The dual republic — Europe's largest state, with elected kings and the Warsaw Confederation's religious tolerance.

properties.name: Kalmar Union
properties.description: Personal union of Denmark, Norway and Sweden under one crown.

properties.name: Teutonic Order State
properties.description: Crusading knight-state on the Baltic; defeated at Grunwald.

properties.name: Kingdom of Hungary
properties.description: Central European kingdom that held the Danube basin until Mohács.

properties.name: Serbian Empire
properties.description: Dušan's short-lived empire of the central Balkans.

properties.name: Ottoman Empire (Rise)
properties.description: The ghazi beylik that grew from a frontier emirate into conqueror of the Balkans.

properties.name: Ottoman Empire (Classical)
properties.description: The Porte at its height: from Hungary to Yemen and Algiers, the Ottomans controlled the eastern Mediterranean.

properties.name: Ottoman Empire (Late)
properties.description: The retreating 'Sick Man of Europe', reformed by Tanzimat yet dismantled after 1918.

properties.name: Habsburg Monarchy
properties.description: The Austrian branch that ruled the Danubian lands, Bohemia and Hungary after Mohács.

properties.name: Austrian Empire
properties.description: The Habsburgs' formal empire of Austria, Bohemia, Hungary and northern Italy.

properties.name: Austria-Hungary
properties.description: The Dual Monarchy — one of Europe's great powers, dissolved after the First World War.

properties.name: Swedish Empire
properties.description: Stormaktstiden — Sweden's Baltic dominion after the Thirty Years' War.

properties.name: Tsardom of Russia
properties.description: Ivan the Terrible's realm that expanded across Siberia to the Pacific.

properties.name: Russian Empire
properties.description: From the Baltic to the Pacific and Alaska — the empire of Peter, Catherine and the Romanovs.

properties.name: Kingdom of Prussia
properties.description: The Hohenzollern military monarchy that unified Germany.

properties.name: British Empire
properties.description: The largest empire in history; on this Europe-centred map only the home islands and Mediterranean outposts are shown.

properties.name: Spanish Empire
properties.description: Habsburg and Bourbon Spain — European hegemon whose overseas empire stretched from the Americas to the Philippines.

properties.name: Portuguese Empire
properties.description: The first global maritime empire; on this map only metropolitan Portugal is shown.

properties.name: Dutch Republic
properties.description: The United Provinces — maritime, mercantile and the seat of the first stock exchange.

properties.name: First French Empire
properties.description: Napoleon's Grande Empire — France, Italy, the Low Countries and the Confederation of the Rhine.

properties.name: German Empire
properties.description: The Second Reich — unified Germany as Europe's leading industrial and military power.

properties.name: Kingdom of Italy
properties.description: The Savoyard kingdom forged by the Risorgimento.

properties.name: Kingdom of Greece
properties.description: Modern Greece from independence through the Balkan Wars to the monarchy's end.

properties.name: Kingdom of Serbia
properties.description: The Piedmont of the South Slavs, whose victory in the Balkan Wars doubled its territory.

properties.name: Yugoslavia
properties.description: The South Slav union — Kingdom, then socialist federation, until its violent breakup.

properties.name: Second Polish Republic
properties.description: Interwar Poland, restored after 123 years of partition.

properties.name: Soviet Union
properties.description: The communist superpower that dominated eastern Europe after 1945.

properties.name: Nazi Germany
properties.description: Hitler's Third Reich — at its height in 1942 it ruled from the Atlantic to the Volga.

properties.name: Fascist Italy
properties.description: Mussolini's Italy — the first fascist state, with Albania annexed in 1939.

properties.name: Russian Federation
properties.description: The largest state on earth, spanning eleven time zones.

properties.name: European Union
properties.description: A supranational union of 27 member states — the modern heir to centuries of European integration.

properties.name: France (Republic)
properties.description: The French Republic from the Third Republic to the Fifth.

properties.name: Germany (Federal Republic)
properties.description: Reunified Germany — the EU's largest economy.

properties.name: Spain (Kingdom)
properties.description: Modern Spain, a constitutional monarchy and EU member.

properties.name: Italy (Republic)
properties.description: The Italian Republic, a founding EU member.

properties.name: Poland (Republic)
properties.description: Post-communist Poland, NATO and EU member.

properties.name: Ukraine
properties.description: Independent Ukraine, Europe's second-largest country by area.

properties.name: United Kingdom
properties.description: The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland — former imperial metropole.
